findings.title: Mixed cash/electronic checkout cannot confirm its electronic leg
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: CheckoutOrderHandler.cs (line 148) posts the cash tender leg using idempotency key 'sale-{CheckoutRequestId}'. When ConfirmElectronicPaymentHandler.cs (line 75) attempts to post the deferred electronic split leg, it attempts to insert into EfFinancialJournal using the exact same key 'sale-{CheckoutRequestId}', throwing a unique constraint violation.
findings.impact: Split payment completion failure. Cash is accepted and deposited into the drawer, but the electronic leg (InstaPay/Card) can never be confirmed on the server; the order remains stuck in pending payment state.
findings.remediation_plan: Key journal entries by stable leg identity, e.g. 'sale-{CheckoutRequestId}-{TenderType}'. Transition pending electronic leg atomically to confirmed.
required_tests: Mixed cash+InstaPay and card+Wallet checkout, confirmation, retry, and concurrent confirm; verify exact tender totals and one movement per leg.
Replay same request and verify stable movement identity.
acceptance_criteria: Each tender leg can complete independently and exactly once.
Confirmed electronic state and its movement commit atomically; channel totals reconcile.

findings.title: Cancelling pending mixed electronic payment hides collected cash without reversal
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: Order.cs:CancelElectronicPayment sets order Status to Cancelled without issuing a reversal journal entry for cash tender legs that were already deposited into the till drawer at checkout.
findings.impact: Treasury divergence. Drawer cash remains physically and logically deposited, but order disappears from sales reports, causing shift drawer reconciliation discrepancies.
findings.remediation_plan: When cancelling a mixed tender order, check if any cash leg was deposited and atomically post a reversal journal movement to the drawer.
required_tests: Cancel cash+electronic and card+electronic orders; reconcile treasury, operational cash, and reports.
Race cancel against confirm and require one terminal tender outcome.
Verify refund only when funds are actually returned.
acceptance_criteria: Cancelled order/payment state preserves every collected tender until a matching reversal exists.
Order, tender, treasury, and report totals reconcile after either winning race.

findings.title: Refund can debit money for an order that was never collected
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: Order.cs:ApplyRefund and RefundOrderHandler.cs do not verify that the order was actually settled (IsPaid == true) before approving a cash refund.
findings.impact: Cash drain. An operator can issue a cash refund against an unpaid Cash-On-Delivery order or pending InstaPay order, draining drawer funds for money never collected.
findings.remediation_plan: Enforce invariant in Order.ApplyRefund that order must be fully collected (IsPaid == true) and refund amount cannot exceed collected tender.
required_tests: Unpaid COD, pending electronic, confirmed paid, partial collected, and unsupported mixed cases.
Race refund with cancel/confirm and concurrent refunds; rejected cases create no refund/movement and balances remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Cumulative refunds never exceed the order’s actually settled amount per tender leg.
Rejected unpaid refund leaves no partial writes; valid refund atomically records refund and outflow.

findings.title: Historical cash refund omitted from current-shift expected cash
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: Drawer mixes lifetime order net amounts with selected operational movement types and does not allocate refunds by OperationalShiftId.
findings.impact: A cash refund executed during current shift B for a sale from shift A may reduce lifetime/order net while the drawer reconciliation for B omits the refund outflow or allocates it to the original sale; expected cash and actual drawer diverge.
findings.remediation_plan: Compute drawer flow from posted operational cash movements or join refund rows by OperationalShiftId; avoid double deduction for same-shift refunds and preserve immutable closed shift snapshots. Separate original sale period from refund execution period.
required_tests: Historical shift A sale refunded in B; verify B actual/expected and final close balance reconcile.
Same-shift partial cash refund counted exactly once.
Historic noncash refund and cross-business-day reports preserve attribution; idempotent retry.
acceptance_criteria: Each refund cash outflow appears once in the shift/business period in which it was executed.
Historical closed shift snapshot remains immutable; current operational drawer reconciles to movements.

findings.title: Concurrent distinct invoice settlements can overpay supplier and corrupt invoice cache
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: PayPurchaseHandler.cs (lines 59-74) reads supplier invoice balance without UPDLOCK or serializable isolation, allowing concurrent transactions to each read the remaining balance before either updates it.
findings.impact: Supplier overpayment and invoice balance corruption under concurrent settlement clicks.
findings.remediation_plan: Execute invoice settlement within an explicit Serializable transaction or apply pessimistic locking (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK) on the purchasing invoice record.
required_tests: Barrier: two different 80 settlements against outstanding 100, both same account and different accounts; at most one succeeds, total <=100 and cache equals ledger.
Same request replay returns committed result.
acceptance_criteria: For each invoice, committed settlements never exceed current outstanding.
Cached paid/outstanding fields match ledger under serialized settlements.
Retries remain idempotent and deadlock policy is bounded.

findings.title: Generic payroll transition marks run Paid without paying treasury or employee ledger
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: TransitionPayrollHandler.cs permits generic status transition of an approved payroll run directly to 'Paid' without generating corresponding treasury journal disbursements or employee ledger settlement entries.
findings.impact: Payroll status marked Paid without actual money leaving treasury or settling employee balances.

required_tests: Generic Approved->Paid is rejected and writes nothing.
Dedicated pay atomically creates expected movement and each settlement.
Actor without payroll_pay cannot set Paid through generic route.
Concurrent cancel/pay results in exactly one consistent terminal state.
acceptance_criteria: Paid status is equivalent to completed committed payout effects.
No API path can mark paid without required payroll_pay authorization and all financial rows.

findings.title: Backup filenames collide within a second and WITH FORMAT can overwrite prior backup
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.
findings.root_cause: Second-resolution timestamp treated as unique filename; no GUID/exclusive reservation. Retention reasons over records not unique physical paths.
findings.impact: Two backup creations within timestamp resolution can target the same physical filename; later WITH FORMAT may overwrite a previously recorded backup or fail, while retention may count multiple records for one path.
findings.remediation_plan: Use collision-resistant immutable backup identity and exclusive create/no-overwrite destination semantics; preserve record-to-file identity. Retention should validate distinct canonical paths and never delete a file still referenced by a retained record.
required_tests: Parallel same-time filename generation returns distinct IDs/paths.
Existing destination collision refuses overwrite.
Retention with duplicate path references preserves all retained valid backups.
Later isolated SQL/media test only with explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria: Each successful backup record resolves to a unique immutable artifact.
A collision cannot silently overwrite a prior artifact; retention cannot delete a retained target.

findings.title: Restore pending-journal check does not exclude active or newly accepted financial work
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.
findings.root_cause: Pending journal staged and completed before common SaveChanges cannot reliably reveal in-flight work; a count snapshot is not writer exclusion. Restore does not put API/print/background writers into maintenance barrier.
findings.impact: Restore’s pending-journal check does not exclude active or newly accepted writes. Restore may enter SINGLE_USER/replace while acknowledged financial operation or background writer is in flight; recovery of latest acknowledged work is not assured by the current check.
findings.remediation_plan: Use a database-backed maintenance admission lease respected by all mutating handlers and background workers; drain in-flight operations, pause workers, take safety backup, restore and verify, clear stale pools/caches/sessions as designed, then resume only after durable outcome recording.
required_tests: Pure coordinator test: after maintenance lease acquired, new writes are rejected and prior writes drained.
Dedicated disposable instance restore with approved fault injection and proof of last acknowledged sale recovery.
Exercise job/API writers and restore failures; never use user-active database.
acceptance_criteria: Restore cannot begin until writers are excluded/drained.
Every accepted operation is either included in pre-restore safety point or has an explicit replay/recovery record.
Failure leaves a known healthy database and maintenance mode controlled.

findings.title: Concurrent different open-day requests create multiple active business days
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.
findings.root_cause: Single-active invariant protected only by read check; no shared singleton lock or unique active-day representation.
findings.impact: Concurrent requests with distinct open-day IDs can both pass read-before-write admission, leaving multiple active business days; queries/gates selecting first active day may attach new finance to inconsistent periods.
findings.remediation_plan: Represent single active ownership with a database-enforced singleton/unique active-state key acquired transactionally by open and reopen. Reconcile existing duplicate active rows explicitly before constraint migration; make read gate fail closed if invariant is corrupt.
required_tests: Concurrent opens with distinct IDs: exactly one active day; same request replay returns same day.
Race reopen versus open; exactly one active day.
Corrupt duplicate fixture makes gate fail closed and emits diagnosable error.
acceptance_criteria: At most one active day exists across app processes.
Open/reopen admission and all active-day readers use the same ownership invariant.

findings.title: Collected sales report drops immediate money from pending mixed payments
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.
findings.root_cause: Any pending electronic leg triggers subtraction of whole order total, instead of pending leg amount; report contradicts own cash channel totals.
findings.impact: Sales report may subtract full order amount while an electronic leg is pending even though immediate cash/card leg was collected, understating collected sales/revenue and contradicting channel reconciliation.
findings.remediation_plan: Compute pending collection as the pending leg amount(s) and separately report gross/net sale recognition from tender settlement timing. Do not infer collection solely from order IsPaid or subtract whole order for partial pending tender.
required_tests: Mixed cash/electronic and card/electronic pending: collected amount equals immediate leg and pending equals deferred leg.
After confirm, totals conserve order amount across channels.
Compare report totals to treasury movements and payment query for each state.
acceptance_criteria: For each order, collected plus pending amounts reconcile to eligible tender total; no collected leg disappears while another awaits confirmation.

findings.title: Shift opening and purchase receipt check protected account balance before their transactions
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK loader invoked before BeginTransaction; statement-end implicit transaction releases lock, balance snapshot stale at spending. SingleOpen index protects only shift rows.
findings.impact: Shift opening float and/or purchase receipt may authorize against stale Main account balance because protective lock query occurs before transaction; competing outflow may spend same available funds, potentially allowing negative pooled account or failed/partial admission.
findings.remediation_plan: Start transaction before protected account balance load/check and hold lock through float/receipt writes; establish consistent account/shift/invoice lock order; make retries safe and preserve real concurrency errors.
required_tests: Barrier-controlled open-float versus withdrawal/expense/purchase distinct requests; account never negative and exactly feasible operation set commits.
Same open request replay and single-active-shift invariant still hold.
Verify purchase receipt document/inventory/financial rows atomic.
acceptance_criteria: Protected balance read and spend are in one transaction with effective lock lifetime.
No successful concurrent commits exceed available balance; rejected command has no partial effects.

findings.title: Attendance correction credits do not enter calculated payroll
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: Correction records signed Adjustment entries; payroll includes Adjustment debits only, with no credit earnings bucket.
findings.impact: A positive attendance correction recorded as Adjustment credit may be ignored by payroll’s included earnings/deduction categories, so the corrected employee period net can remain lower than ledger balance.
findings.remediation_plan: Reconcile both credit and debit sides of Adjustment into payroll net; preserve correction attribution and original earning basis if required; keep payroll freeze semantics explicit.
required_tests: Payroll input with prior Deduction debit plus correcting Adjustment credit restores expected net.
Attendance correction followed by payroll calculation and report agrees with employee ledger.
Correction before run creation and after run freeze follow documented policy.
acceptance_criteria: Every eligible period employee-ledger credit/debit included exactly once in payroll liability.
Payroll line and ledger are consistent; post-freeze correction follows explicit reopen/adjustment policy.

findings.title: Owner dashboard adds outgoing stock instead of subtracting it
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: OwnerDashboardQueryService.cs calculates inventory stock movements by summing QuantityMilliUnits without multiplying by -1 when Direction == Out.
findings.impact: Inventory stock overstatement on owner dashboard. Waste and sales increase stock totals rather than decreasing them.
findings.remediation_plan: Apply proper sign negation: (m.Direction == StockMovementDirection.Out ? -m.QuantityMilliUnits : m.QuantityMilliUnits).
required_tests: Seed positive-magnitude In and Out movements plus count adjustments/waste; dashboard balance and low-stock set equal inventory overview.
Cover zero/negative normalized inputs and multiple movement kinds.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard stock projection equals canonical inventory balance for every item.
Out never increases available quantity; count corrections are treated per shared domain rule.

findings.title: Restore success followed by MULTI_USER failure is classified as database not replaced
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.
findings.root_cause: databaseWasReplaced becomes true only after RESTORE and MULTI_USER both return. If restore159 succeeded and MULTI_USER164 throws/cancels, catch releases mode best-effort but leaves false flag and Failed status.
findings.impact: Operator may be told restore failed after database replacement; RecordOutcome false branch does not re-add disappeared restore row or clear killed connection pool. Incorrect outcome can encourage a dangerous retry. Actual failure at this precise boundary has not been produced.
findings.remediation_plan: Track restore replacement separately from recovery/availability state; persist explicit replaced-but-recovery-incomplete outcome outside replaced database. Resolve uncertain SQL acknowledgments through a recovery protocol; do not auto-retry destructive restore.
required_tests: Fake coordinator injects failure/cancellation after RESTORE but before/during MULTI_USER.
Approved disposable-instance fault injection verifies replaced database is never reported untouched and no automatic retry occurs.
acceptance_criteria: Restore command outcome distinguishes database replacement from return to MULTI_USER/availability; partial success is durably recorded outside replaced DB.
Injected post-RESTORE mode failure never reports database untouched and never triggers automatic retry.

findings.title: Checkout can commit after its previously open shift has completed handover
findings.confidence: HIGH for missing in-transaction shift revalidation in approved source; concrete SQL acceptance predicted under stated normal schema, not runtime observed.
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: Open shift predicate read before checkout transaction is not revalidated/held through commit; closing uses a different correctly locked Shift update that checkout does not perform.
findings.impact: Recorded closed shift expected/actual/handover exclude newly committed cash order while order and posted drawer collection reference that closed shift; new order time can be later than ClosedAtUtc. Stock can also be consumed when configured. No cash loss, fraud, exploit, or accepted real write observed.
findings.remediation_plan: Serialize checkout admission and shift close with a shared transaction-held Shift row protocol: lock/revalidate Open before writes, hold through commit; alternatively use a documented Closing/drain process. Preserve closed snapshots.
required_tests: Barrier after checkout shift read and before transaction; close then resume checkout: reject with zero order/payment/stock effects.
Reverse ordering: checkout admission held; close waits and includes sale.
Same-key replay after close remains nonmutating.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh checkout and shift close serialize through shared shift admission; every accepted checkout is included in handover or rejected with no effects.
Same-key replay after close remains idempotent and nonmutating.

findings.title: Unvalidated signed delivery fee can bypass intended discount and comp authorization
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: CheckoutOrderHandler.cs (line 142) accepts request.DeliveryFeePiastres directly from client payload without verifying against DeliveryService.DefaultFee or checking manager authorization.

findings.remediation_plan: Validate delivery fee server-side against configured delivery rates or require manager override for non-standard delivery fees.
required_tests: Negative fee with ordinary POS actor; overflow boundaries; assert no writes.
Positive/zero fee, tax, approved comp, COD and legitimate discounts.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid signed fee and arithmetic overflow rejected before any order, stock, journal or treasury write.
Valid positive/zero fees and approved discount/comp routes retain policy behavior.

findings.title: Financial approval provenance can retain unvalidated shift presenter or discard verified driver variance approver
findings.disposition_rationale: Source behavior is deterministic but depends on owner business policy (e.g. tax rounding policy, legacy casing tolerance, packaging cost allocation).
findings.root_cause: Financial attribution derives from presentation or earlier base gate rather than the actual verified relevant authorization result. Original shift evidence and related driver variance variant are preserved separately.
findings.impact: False attribution to a person who did not issue approval; no money change or otherwise forbidden operation authorized by this defect alone.
findings.remediation_plan: Carry verified gate result, actor, and actual approver identity separately to all financial rows/audit; preserve OR authorization policy and approval reason semantics.
required_tests: Direct-permission below-threshold unnecessary presenter; above-threshold approved variance; verify actor/approver on movement, close event, settlement and audit.
Wrong action/consumed approval and permission-only actor controls.
acceptance_criteria: Persisted approver attribution is the verified approver for the actual gate; actor and approver are distinct fields where required.
Below-threshold optional presentation cannot be misattributed; above-threshold approval still enforces approval action, reason, and amount.

findings.title: Negative receipt quantity and unit cost can post stock reduction with supplier debt
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.
findings.root_cause: Aggregate payment validation substituted for per-line positive receipt quantity/nonnegative purchase cost validation.
findings.impact: Incorrect stock reduction labelled receipt and positive supplier debt for invalid purchase; unauthorized privilege escalation not claimed.

Positive receipt and distinct authorized return flow.
acceptance_criteria: Receipt rejects unsupported negative quantity/unit-cost combinations before posting stock or supplier debt.
Valid positive receipts and any approved return/credit workflow remain coherent and atomic.

findings.title: Pending mixed delivery includes already collected payment leg in driver custody
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified directly against current baseline source code. Flaw logic, call path, and impact independently confirmed with zero contradictions.
findings.root_cause: Delivery responsibility collapses per-leg payment collection into one whole-order IsPaid flag and Total-refund. Mixed pending order is partially collected, but modeled as wholly uncollected for driver custody.
findings.impact: Overstated driver collection/custody by already posted immediate leg; possible duplicate customer collection or artificial driver variance/approval requirement. No claim actual customer payment, cash theft, SQL acceptance or persisted double revenue was reproduced.
findings.remediation_plan: Use per-tender-leg collection status/amount when deriving driver custody. Do not reinterpret pending electronic receivable as driver cash; block dispatch or provide an explicit owner-approved conversion/recovery workflow.
required_tests: Mixed immediate cash/card plus pending electronic dispatch; assert custody does not include collected leg or silently convert pending claim.
All-immediate Multi and cash COD positive controls; explicit conversion policy only if approved.
acceptance_criteria: Driver custody equals only currently collectible amounts under documented payment contract; pending electronic leg is never silently converted to cash owed.
Block or explicitly convert pending leg only under owner-approved flow, with atomic custody/movement/reporting.

findings.title: First stock receipt can race unit-change admission and reinterpret movement history
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.

Current stock display joins current Unit, and valuation/recipe conversions can become semantically inconsistent; no measured monetary loss or actual SQL schedule executed.
findings.remediation_plan: Coordinate unit edits and first movement admission through a shared DB transaction lock/revision invariant used by both edit and every movement writer. Version only works if both paths participate.
required_tests: Barrier first movement admission vs unit change; ensure at most one incompatible operation commits.
Sequential post-first-movement unit change rejection and legitimate same-unit metadata update.
acceptance_criteria: A unit change and first movement cannot both pass against same pre-movement state; one is rejected or serialized.
All readers continue to interpret historical movements using stable unit semantics.

Ensure old orders frozen.

Historical frozen orders unchanged; new checkout and estimate agree under enabled nonzero rate.

findings.title: Distinct employee credit requests can persist and display stale running-balance snapshots

Same-key retry, rollback/restart, same-command pending rows, payout lock ordering, equal timestamp tie.

Same-key replay, pending same-command rows, and locked payout remain correct; tie ordering is deterministic.

Client control-center-only access sees no financial figures; permitted report viewer still accesses.

Unauthorized session receives no financial snapshot payload; authorized reader can still access permitted history.

Mismatched actor/employee/amount conflict; concurrent same-key SQL test only in approved disposable DB.

findings.title: JSON actor casing mismatch permits body-selected authorization identity

Minimal API model binding in Program.cs (lines 1951-1958) binds case-insensitively into UpdateUserPermissionsRequest.ActorUserId. 1. In AuthenticationMiddleware.cs, parse request body using case-insensitive property name matching (e.g. EnumerateObject() with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase).
2. Refactor Program.cs endpoint and UpdateUserPermissionsHandler to eliminate ActorUserId from wire DTOs and bind authorized caller identity exclusively from context.ActorId() established by token session resolution.

Verify UpdateUserPermissionsHandler authorizes against authenticated session user even if body attempts to provide ActorUserId.

findings.title: Distinct concurrent business-day opens can pass pre-insert active-state validation
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.
findings.root_cause: Active-day admission is a read-check-insert invariant. OpenBusinessDayHandler reads current active rows and invokes BusinessDayRules.Open before a separate insert; there is no shared transaction/conditional state claim, while the schema has uniqueness only by request ID.

findings.remediation_plan: Confirm the invariant scope. If one active BusinessDay is intended, enforce it at the same persistence boundary as the single-open-shift invariant (provider-appropriate active-row uniqueness or a serialized admission row/lock covering Open and Reopen), and make losing admission return a stable conflict without partial side effects. Preserve same-request idempotency. Do not rely solely on a pre-insert read.
required_tests: Barrier-controlled concurrent opens with two distinct RequestIds: at most one active day commits; loser receives a conflict and no second row is created.
Same RequestId replay returns the original day without a second row.
Concurrent reopen of one day and open of another cannot create two active days if global invariant is confirmed.
Sequential open while Open, Closing, or Reopened rejects; after valid close, a new day opens.
Run against supported SQL Server provider and two independent DbContext/process instances; assert database-level invariant.
acceptance_criteria: A documented owner policy establishes the active-day scope (global or per defined partition).

If global single-active-day remains intended, every Open/Reopen transition is serialized or constrained by database-enforced uniqueness so concurrent instances cannot persist more than one active day.
A losing concurrency attempt leaves no partial state and the existing same-request replay contract remains intact.
